description.narrative: The project will assist the Government of Cambodia to (i) modernize and improve the climate and disaster resilience of four irrigation systems in Battambang, Kampong Cham, Kampong Thom, and Takeo provinces to supply water to 43,500 hectares (ha) for 291,847 people, of whom 148,288 (51%) are women; (ii) ensure sustainability of these irrigation schemes by strengthening the institutional and financial capacity of the government staff and farmer water user communities (FWUCs) in operation and maintenance (O&M); (iii) improve farming practices for increased agricultural productivity and crop diversification; and (iv) establish a national water resources data management center (NWRDMC), a water resources information system (WRIS), and an irrigation asset management system for better water resources management, planning, operations, and investment.

Output: Efficiency and climate resilience of irrigation systems enhanced Indicator: Achieving 50% collection rate of the irrigation service fee Data Source: QPRs of the executing agency and PPMS Actual value:

Output: Efficiency and climate resilience of irrigation systems enhanced Indicator: At least 200 demonstration plots on climate-resilient farming practices and crop diversification established with the four subprojects Achievement: 122 Progress/Status: A total of 122 farm demonstrations have been completed, representing 61% of the target. Data Source: QPRs of the executing agency and PPMS

Output: Efficiency and climate resilience of irrigation systems enhanced Indicator: At least one irrigation asset management system functioning Progress/Status: The Irrigation Asset Management System (IAMS) design is agreed and the IAMS system is under development and tested. The progress is 85%. Data Source: QPRs of the executing agency and PPMS Actual value:

Output: Efficiency and climate resilience of irrigation systems enhanced Indicator: Women comprise at least 40% of participants in all project-supported training on climate-resilient farming practices, crop diversification, and water management Achievement: 39 Progress/Status: Prek Po FWUC, 10 Farmers Groups in Stung Chinit Spillway and 2 FWUGs in Stung Chinit Spillway of these two sub-projects have been trained on the farm preparation, field visits and demo sites for 313 times with 1,885 persons, including 729 females (38.67%) from 14 December 2021 to 21 March 2025.
The topics were included: 1. Analysis rice value chain 2. Training on SRP. 3. Conservation awareness 4. Millers Producers Group 5. Contract Farming 6. Farmers field day and study tours 7. Rice farming techniques 8. Seed producers' group 9. Groups Mgt Plan 10. Monitoring & coaching rice seed producers. 11. Gender Action Learning System 12. Bookkeeping training. Data Source: QPRs of the executing agency and PPMS
